chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufaddal al-Ju'fi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The anguish, the regret, and the woe, all of it is for the one who does not benefit from what he sees and does not know what the matter is upon which he is standing, whether it is beneficial for him or harmful.' I said to him, 'So by what would the saved ones be recognized from these people? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'The one whose deed is in accordance with his words, to him the testimony of salvation is affirmed; and the one whose deed is not in accordance with his words, then that is merely the lending (of faith).'

key_terms.الْمُسْتَوْدَع: The lent one (referring to temporary faith)

ai.seo_question: How can one distinguish between true believers and those with superficial faith according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between genuine faith (*Iman*) and mere nominal belief by emphasizing the congruence of action with declaration. He asserts that those whose deeds align with their words are guaranteed salvation, whereas those whose actions contradict their claims possess only 'lent' faith (*Emarat al-Iman*), which is temporary and liable to withdrawal. This concept highlights the Shia scholarly view that true faith is validated through practical consistency rather than verbal assertion alone.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Mufazzal Al Ju’fy who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The anguish, and the regret and the woe, all of it is for the one who does not benefit from what he sees and does not know what the matter is which he is standing upon, is it beneficial for him or harmful?’ I said to himasws, ‘So by what would the saved ones be recognised from them, may I be sacrificed for youasws?’ Heasws said: ‘The one whose deed was in accordance to his words, so the testimony of the salvation would be affirmed for him, and the one whose deed does not happen to be in accordance to his words, so rather, that is the temporary one (of the Emān)’.
en.sarwar: 1. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal al-Ju’fl who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Sorrow, regret and lamentation strikes one who does not benefit from what he sees and does not know upon what ground is he standing; is it beneficial for him or harmful?’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, by what means are the ones who have found salvation recognized?’ The Imam said, ‘One whose acts agree with his words, testimony for his salvation holds true and one whose deeds do not agree with his words, his belief is transient. ’”
